mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan Investing Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Special cross-strait path: Taiwan judicial notary public notarization -> Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification -> Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) or provincial notary association verification -> submission to PRC SAMR. Not Hague Apostille because Taiwan is not an Apostille Contracting State; not PRC consular legalization because no consular relations exist.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Registration Facts) of the Taiwan Investing Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Special cross-strait path: Taiwan judicial notary public notarization -> SEF verification -> ARATS or provincial notary association verification -> submission to PRC SAMR and the target WFOE's future bank. This path is parallel to and mutually exclusive from Hague Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Taiwan Investing Company and Power of Attorney for WFOE Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notarized by a Taiwan judicial notary public after adoption by the Taiwan investing company's board of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public notarization -> SEF verification -> ARATS or provincial notary association verification -> delivery to the PRC corporate service agent and SAMR. No Hague Apostille and no consular legalization are chained to this sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Articles of Association (Charter) of the Taiwan Investing Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs / registered corporate secretarial office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Special cross-strait path: Taiwan judicial notary public notarization -> SEF verification -> ARATS or provincial notary association verification -> submission to PRC SAMR and the commercial bank. This authentication path is a non-Hague, non-consular parallel mechanism unique to cross-strait document legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Taiwan Investing Company's Principal Settlement Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan-based commercial bank holding the investing company's operating accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan bank officer's signature notarized by a Taiwan judicial notary public -> SEF verification -> ARATS or provincial notary association verification -> submission to the PRC target bank and registration authority. This is not an apostille or consular legalization path; it is the mandatory cross-strait verification mechanism.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation, screen every ultimate beneficial owner, director, shareholder, and authorized signatory against (i) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN) and non-SDN sanctions lists; (iii) UK HMT and EU consolidated financial sanctions lists; (iv) PRC law-enforcement, PBOC anti-money laundering risk lists, and the Unreliable Entity List; and (v) Taiwan competent authority financial action task force publications. Mandatory risk-based enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons (PEPs), including mainland Chinese and Taiwan officials, their family members and close associates, covering source of wealth and source of funds for any proposed capital contribution. Ongoing monitoring must continue for at least 12 months after bank account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Application and Registration Service Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be in simplified Chinese characters. A four-tier naming structure is mandatory: administrative division, distinctive trade name (zihao), industry or business description, and legal form such as Co., Ltd. The trade name must contain at least two Chinese characters and may be a phonetic or semantic transliteration of the foreign investor's name. Pure Latin letters, Arabic numerals alone, or pinyin-only names are not registrable as the legal name; an English auxiliary name is permitted only as a non-registered trade designation. SAMR review enforces public order, national security, and anti-confusion doctrines.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An applicant may extend a name reservation once for a further 30 days by filing electronically before the initial 30-day reservation window expires. If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration with the next higher-level market regulator within 15 working days of the rejection decision, citing the Enterprise Name Registration Administration Provisions. Alternatively, the applicant may institute an administrative lawsuit before the competent people's court within six months of the rejection. The appeal must attach all previously submitted name application records and a comparative legal analysis showing that the rejected name does not violate public order or national security.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a WFOE engaged in retailing smart IoT devices and home automation hardware, a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected by PRC tax authorities and major Chinese banks for tax registration and bank account opening because the business license must reflect a fixed physical business premise. Some free trade zones permit cluster registration with a designated zone-provided address, but local tax authorities and banks require actual operating premises, evidence of lease, rent invoices, and on-site verification before issuing invoices or processing foreign exchange. Home-based or mail-forwarding-only virtual offices are not permissible for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-high, approximately 35% probability in the first 12 months of operation. Checklist: (1) original lease contract and property ownership certificate; (2) rent payment receipts and bank payment records; (3) on-site staff presence and identity documentation; (4) company signboard matching the registered name; (5) inventory or working equipment consistent with smart-home device retail; (6) electricity and utility invoices in the company name; (7) complete statutory books and records. Municipal tax bureaus and SAMR conduct double-random, one-open unannounced inspections; failure can lead to administrative penalties and revocation of registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), administered nationally through the China Electronic Tax Bureau online portal (Electronic Taxpayer/e-Tax system) at etax.chinatax.gov.cn and provincial-level tax service offices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation, the WFOE obtains an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); the USCC is the statutory taxpayer identification number for Chinese tax purposes. The SAMR shares the incorporation data with the STA under the multi-license integration mechanism, and the WFOE must then activate its tax account through the Electronic Tax Bureau within 30 calendar days after the business license issuance, submitting the business license, articles of association, registered address, legal representative identity documents, capital contribution records, and finance and accounting system details. The tax authority activates the VAT taxpayer profile, determines small-scale or general VAT taxpayer status, assigns invoice quotas, and links payroll, social insurance, stamp duty, and other filing modules. A foreign non-resident entity without a permanent establishment in China that derives China-source income or makes taxable supplies in China must separately obtain a non-resident taxpayer TIN by completing the non-resident enterprise registration or withholding-agent registration with the competent STA office through the Electronic Tax Bureau, supported by the home-country certificate of incorporation, the China-source contract or invoice, and the appointed withholding agent's tax registration details. The WFOE itself uses its own USCC as its TIN and does not rely on the foreign parent's TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the WFOE is a Chinese tax-resident limited liability enterprise subject to Enterprise Income Tax at entity level on worldwide income; no pass-through or transparent classification is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - China does not maintain a check-the-box entity classification election, and no domestic hybrid mismatch election exists for WFOEs. The WFOE may elect general VAT taxpayer treatment if it meets the statutory conditions, but this is an indirect-tax status election, not an entity classification. Anti-avoidance rules and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule may deny any purported mismatch benefit.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the People's Republic of China VAT system, including special and ordinary VAT invoices and the export tax rebate (exemption and refund) mechanism.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales - this threshold triggers mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration and access to input VAT credit. The WFOE must register for tax from establishment regardless of turnover; there is no economic registration threshold for a resident company, while smaller taxable persons below the threshold may be small-scale taxpayers subject to the simplified levy rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates issuance of VAT invoices through the STA-controlled electronic invoice service platform under the fully digitalised electronic invoice reform. Every valid invoice receives a unique tax-authority invoice number and a digital fiscal stamp, and invoice data is transmitted in real time to the STA's Golden-Tax information system. Special VAT invoices and ordinary invoices must be issued using the approved electronic invoice modules or API integrations; the tax authority validates invoice issuance for anti-fraud purposes, reconciles sales information, and links customs export data through the China International Trade Single Window. Paper-only or off-platform invoicing is not a lawful clearance method for VAT purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A WFOE that is a VAT general taxpayer may apply the zero percent export VAT rate (exemption and refund) to tangible smart-home IoT hardware that physically leaves mainland China customs territory, including exports to Taiwan, provided the sale is a true cross-border supply, title passes to the overseas buyer, the goods are declared to customs as exports, and the export proceeds are received and repatriated in accordance with State Administration of Foreign Exchange rules. Qualifying digital offshore services are separately subject to cross-border service zero-rating; IoT hardware retail is not a service. The export must be supported by matching shipping, customs, commercial, and payment documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Customs Export Goods Declaration (export bill of entry / customs release record generated through the China International Trade Single Window)
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical cross-border shipment to the foreign or Taiwan consignee
Commercial invoice and packing list identical in commodity description, quantity, value, and consignee to the customs declaration
Export sales contract or purchase order
Foreign exchange repatriation certificate (bank-issued export proceeds receipt confirmation and SAFE goods-trade monitoring record, serving the inward remittance certificate function)
Proof of export tax rebate eligibility, including VAT invoice records and inventory/production traceability where required by the STA
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day statutory window, or if the customs, transport, commercial, or foreign-exchange documents fail to substantiate the physical export, the STA reclassifies the sale as a domestic taxable supply, charges VAT at the applicable standard rate (normally 13%), assesses late-payment surcharge, and recovers any previously refunded input VAT. For fraudulent or unverified export refund claims, the STA may impose a fine of 50 percent to five times the tax refunded or evaded under the Law on Administration of Tax Collection and Levy, and confirmed export-refund fraud may be referred for criminal prosecution for tax fraud; the STA and customs also use export-tax-rebate risk classification and stop refunds for high-risk enterprises until documentation, logistics, and foreign-exchange transactions are fully verified.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), the Foreign Exchange Administration authority operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates a carefully administered partial-convertibility system. The RMB is fully convertible on the current account for genuine trade and service transactions, subject to authenticity verification through SAFE's Trade Monitoring System and the banking system's electronic records. A mainland WFOE may hold a basic CNY settlement account and a foreign currency current account, convert export proceeds into RMB, and remit profits, royalties, salaries, and service fees upon submission of audited financial statements, tax proof, and underlying contracts. Capital account transactions, however, remain restricted and require SAFE registration or approval: inbound equity investment funds must enter a designated capital account, be verified by a certified public accountant, and be used only within the WFOE's approved business scope; foreign debt must be registered and may be constrained by macro-prudential risk parameters. Profit remittance is permissible but demands a cumulative tax clearance certificate and audited accounts. There is no system-wide surrender obligation or fixed conversion ratio for export proceeds; rather, the bank verifies each conversion against customs and logistics data. The overall effect is a 'managed convertibility' framework that supports trade but controls speculative capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency receipts must be repatriated to the WFOE's foreign currency current account in China and reported through SAFE's Trade Monitoring System generally within 180 days from the Customs export declaration date; high-integrity enterprises can benefit from extended facilitation windows. There is no mandatory percentage surrender; the WFOE may retain the foreign currency or sell it to a domestic bank for RMB, but each conversion must be supported by export customs declarations, invoices, logistics documents, and a recognized SAFE transaction purpose code.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low/Not viable as a primary treasury rail. Foreign EMIs such as Stripe, PayPal, Airwallex, and Payoneer are not licensed banks in mainland China and cannot legally open a domestic corporate account or clear CNY inside the onshore RTGS/CIPS system. They may be used offshore for e-commerce receipts into a Hong Kong or overseas subsidiary, but repatriation into the WFOE must occur through a domestic licensed bank under SAFE. Any onshore fintech partner must be a licensed Chinese payment institution operating purely as a collection aggregator; however, cross-border card acquiring for WFOE retail is not a substitute for bank clearing and FX compliance. The WFOE should therefore treat these tools as sales channel utilities only, not as the licensed corporate treasury and FX rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New WFOE account opening generally requires the legal representative or, where properly appointed, a local authorized signatory with a notarized and cross-strait authenticated power of attorney to attend an in-branch interview at the bank's corporate counter. Remote-consular proxy opening is not an established right; most domestic banks allow a remote video verification only as a supplement after the initial biometric/identity verification has been completed in China. For a Taiwanese shareholder, the board resolutions and POA must be notarized and authenticated through the applicable cross-strait document procedure before the bank compliance officer can approve onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Taiwanese shareholder's source of wealth and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain cannot be validated from public records; nominee or shell ownership is suspected.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation and articles of association of the Taiwanese parent; full shareholder register and UBO declaration for any person holding 25% or more, including tax residence and nationalities; audited financial statements for the last two years; bank or investment statements showing the origin of the injected capital; passport copies of all directors; and a notarized/cross-strait authenticated beneficial ownership affidavit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border e-commerce flows from Stripe/Shopify create unexplained mismatches between sales revenue, customs declarations, and banking receipts; trade-based money laundering red flag is triggered.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform settlement reports with SKU-level sales and payout history; export customs declaration records and logistics waybills; inventory purchase invoices and supplier contracts; refund and chargeback reports; bank statements matching every deposit to a platform settlement cycle; and a third-party audit reconciliation tying orders, invoices, shipping documents, and payments together.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Smart home IoT hardware contains embedded encryption, cameras, radio transceivers, or sensors that could be classified as dual-use or controlled items; sanctions or export-control exposure is suspected.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Technology classification memo by an export-control specialist including HS codes and, where applicable, ECCN or China control-list status; end-user and end-use attestations; restricted-party screening results for customers and counterparties; a written internal export compliance policy; and evidence of license or general-license eligibility if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital account funds are co-mingled with operational receipts, or rapid conversion between RMB and foreign currency appears unrelated to real trade; a regulatory filing or SAR is triggered.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI registration certificate; bank record of the separate capital account; CPA capital verification report; board minutes authorizing capital usage; audited use-of-funds statements; and all underlying contracts and orders showing that foreign currency conversions are tied to permitted current account or capital account transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Taiwanese parent remits USD or TWD via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's designated foreign currency capital account at a Chinese licensed bank. The remittance must state the SAFE-coded direct investment purpose (FDI equity injection) and reference the FDI registration certificate. Upon receipt, the bank verifies the MT103 against SAFE's FDI information system; the WFOE must not release funds for conversion until the bank records the inbound investment and a Chinese CPA issues a capital verification report. RMB conversion is executed only when the intended use falls within the approved business scope; the corresponding evidence, including contracts and invoices, must be kept for retrospective compliance. No capital injection may be routed through personal accounts or unauthorized third-party schemes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for inventory and operating imports should use SWIFT MT103 for standard recurring supplier payments in USD/EUR/TWD; large-volume or tightly structured procurements should use commercial letters of credit with a confirming bank to secure payment terms; documentary collections (D/P or D/A) provide a lower-cost alternative for established suppliers. All outbound remittances require underlying purchase contracts, supplier invoices, customs import/export records where goods cross borders, and a SAFE trade-payment purpose code. Where a counterparty accepts RMB, the WFOE may route via CIPS to reduce conversion cost and enhance clearing traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with licensed onshore banks, supported by real trade/current-account or registered capital-account exposure
FX swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for longer-term working-capital or debt hedging, subject to SAFE registration and the real-demand principle

Onshore RMB FX options (plain vanilla call/put) for invoice-level cash-flow hedging; offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally not permissible for an onshore WFOE and may only be considered by an offshore treasury entity when deliverable onshore access is unavailable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder Meeting and Approval of Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company Registration Office, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each fiscal year-end (by June 30 for calendar-year entities); meeting minutes and resolutions must be filed with MOEA only if they trigger registration amendments.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual shareholders meeting within the statutory time frame exposes responsible officers to fines of NTD 10,000 to 50,000 (approx. USD 320 to 1,610). Repeated willful non-compliance can trigger administrative strike-off after formal warning and due process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement Filing (Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (ROC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every calendar year from May 1 to May 31 for the preceding fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 10% of unpaid tax (minimum NTD 20,000 / USD 645) plus monthly late interest of 1.5%. Unfiled taxes may be subject to administrative seizure of assets and forced collection; continued refusal to file can lead to suspension of business or registration strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Substantial Owners (UBO) Declaration under Article 22-1 of the Taiwan Company Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate Registration and Disclosure Platform, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation filed between March 1 and March 31 for the prior year; any change in directors, supervisors, managers, or shareholders holding 10% or more of shares must be reported within 15 calendar days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing, late filing, or false filing subjects the company to penalties ranging from NTD 50,000 to 500,000 (approx. USD 1,610 to 16,130) per enforcement action. Repeated violations after corrective notice may invoke administrative strike-off under the Company Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Mandatory CPA Audit and Certification of Financial Statements (if statutory thresholds are met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Certified Public Accountant (CPA) registered with the Financial Supervisory Commission; audit reports filed with MOEA and tax authorities as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The CPA review and audit opinion must be completed and delivered to the board before the statutory shareholders meeting deadline, normally no later than June 30 for a calendar-year company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to arrange a mandatory CPA audit renders the shareholders meeting approval of financial statements legally defective and can result in MOEA fines of NTD 100,000 to 500,000 (approx. USD 3,230 to 16,130). The company may also lose certain tax incentives and be subject to compulsory strike-off for non-compliance with recording and reporting obligations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit is legally required for a Taiwan company if any one of the following thresholds is exceeded: (a) paid-in capital of at least NTD 30 million (approx. USD 968,000); (b) net operating revenue of at least NTD 100 million (approx. USD 3,226,000); (c) workforce exceeding 100 employees. In addition, all public companies, financial institutions, insurance enterprises, securities firms, and licensed special industries are unconditionally subject to CPA audits. These criteria are set out in the Commercial Accounting Act, the Regulations on Bookkeeping and Financial Statement Certification, and related MOEA announcements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies must apply Taiwan-IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards as endorsed in Taiwan). Non-public companies may apply the Enterprise Accounting Standard (EAS), a simplified local GAAP that is broadly converged with IFRS for SMEs. Consolidated financial statements, when required, are prepared under Taiwan-IFRS or IFRS depending on the regulated status of the company. Tax returns are reconciled separately under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Article 22-1 of the Taiwan Company Act, every company is required to disclose its directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding 10% or more of total shares or capital. The annual confirmation filing must be submitted electronically through the MOEA disclosure platform between March 1 and March 31 of each year, covering data for the preceding calendar year. Any change in these substantial owners or officers must be reported within 15 calendar days of the effective change. The filing is free of charge and constitutes the official annual UBO/ownership confirmation for anti-money-laundering compliance.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - 500 per year (typical registered office/compliance service provider fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - 8,000 (typical certified CPA audit fee for a Taiwan SME once audit thresholds are met)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment tax credits for eligible R&D and green energy projects under the Statute for Industrial Innovation; exemption for retained earnings actually reinvested in productive assets; no general free-zone tax holidays; annual remittance tax of 5% on undistributed earnings subject to specific reinvestment carve-outs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 07 – Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (营利事业所得税结算申报书) e-filed via the Ministry of Finance electronic tax filing portal (tax.nat.gov.tw) using the approved EBK or tax-agent software; mandatory electronic filing for corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due within 5 months after fiscal year-end (for calendar-year taxpayers, May 31; extension only in case of disaster or force majeure).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Line 100 – Gross Revenue (营业收入总额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross sales, service income, and other operating revenue derived from retailing smart IoT and home automation hardware, including cross-border e-commerce sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income attributable to the Taiwan permanent establishment. For online sales to residents by a Taiwan-resident WFOE, full gross revenue must be reported. If any revenue is sourced from a mainland China related party, ensure allocation is consistent with the arm's length principle, and no tax avoidance is achieved through mis-invoicing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 200 – Cost of Goods Sold (销售成本)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs directly attributable to inventory sold, including purchase cost, freight, customs duties, and manufacturing overhead if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When purchasing inventory from non-resident related suppliers (e.g., a mainland China manufacturing affiliate), apply pricing based on TNMM or Cost Plus method. Retain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation to justify the gross margin. If the Taiwan tax authority adjusts the price, the cost deductibility will be denied under Income Tax Act Article 43-1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 300 – Operating Expenses (营业费用)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses, including royalties, service fees, rental, and employee compensation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-residents for royalties or technical services are subject to 20% withholding tax (or 15% for interest). To deduct such expenses, you must (i) withhold and remit the tax timely; (ii) prove actual provision of services and economic substance of the payee; (iii) submit a Form 07A summary of expenses paid to non-residents. Without proper withholding, the expense is non-deductible and may trigger criminal liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Line 400 – Non-operating Income and Expenses (营业外损益)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, dividend income, exchange gains/losses, gains/losses on disposal of assets, and other non-core items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest received from foreign related parties must be at arm's length; if the interest rate is manipulated to shift profit, the tax authority will impute notional interest under Article 43-1. For interest paid to non-residents, apply 15% withholding and ensure the recipient is the beneficial owner; otherwise the rate increases to 20% or the deduction is disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 500 – Taxable Income (课税所得额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after adding back non-deductible expenses and deducting tax-exempt income and prior-year losses within the 10-year carryforward limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This figure must include any transfer pricing adjustments made by the tax authority. If a loss is carried forward, ensure the 'blue return' or CPA-audited certification requirement under Article 39 is satisfied; otherwise the loss may be disallowed. Losses used to offset income generated from non-resident permanent establishments cannot be used against Taiwan-source income unless properly attributed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 600 – Tax Payable after Credits (应纳税额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax computed at 20% of taxable income, reduced by foreign tax credits and eligible investment tax credits, net of any prepaid and withholding tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits on dividends from mainland China subsidiaries may only be claimed if the income is included in the Taiwan return and the DTA (if any) permits indirect tax credit. For dividends distributed to a non-resident shareholder, the company must withhold a 21% dividend withholding tax on the actual disbursement; this withholding is not a credit against the corporate income tax but a separate obligation. Failure to withhold will render the company liable for the unpaid tax and a 3x penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 3% per month on the unpaid tax amount, up to a maximum of 10%. Abatement of failure to file within 3 months: a flat penalty of NT$1,500 to NT$15,000 plus interest at the interbank rate. Fraudulent understatement: penalty of up to twice the underestimated tax under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act. Additionally, responsible directors may be fined NT$50,000 and subject to travel restrictions under Article 24 of the Tax Collection Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (including mainland China investors) under Income Tax Act Article 88; reduced to 0% for resident corporate shareholders (subject to the 5% retained earnings surtax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a bilateral tax treaty (DTA) reduction, a non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the residence jurisdiction; (2) provide a Beneficial Ownership Declaration confirming the recipient has the right to enjoy the dividend and does not pass it through to a third country; (3) file a written application with the Taiwan district tax office before the payment date (or at the latest by the payment date) using Form ‘Application for Exemption/Reduction of Withholding Tax’; (4) receive an approval letter from the tax authority. For mainland China investors, the 2015 Cross-Strait Tax Cooperation Agreement is not yet in force, so no treaty relief is currently available; the full 21% statutory rate applies. In all cases, the payer must retain the approved certificate for audit purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-residents: statutory withholding rate of 15%; treaty-reduced rates generally 10% (e.g., under OECD-style DTAs). Royalties paid to non-residents: statutory withholding rate of 20%; treaty-reduced rates vary (often 10% or 15%). To claim treaty rates, the same TRC and beneficial ownership process as for dividends is required, plus evidence of actual service delivery or IP utilisation. Without treaty relief, the full statutory rate applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: TWD 300 million annual operating revenue threshold; or controlled transactions with related parties reaching TWD 200 million for tangible property transfers; or TWD 50 million for intangible property transfers, service transactions, or capital use/financing transactions. Companies meeting any threshold must prepare a Master File and Local File (TP Report) in Chinese, and file an annual transfer pricing report with the tax return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute of the type seen in commonwealth jurisdictions, but its General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Income Tax Act Article 43-1) and the Supreme Administrative Court doctrine of ‘substantive taxation’ allow the tax authority to re-characterise transactions lacking real economic substance. For treaty relief, the Taiwan tax authority will apply the ‘main purpose test’ under the Multilateral Instrument (where applicable) and will deny benefits if the entity does not perform substantial business activities in the residence state. For intercompany transactions to be respected, the Taiwan entity must show real staff, premises, decision-making, and risk-taking functions (CIGA) commensurate with the income it reports.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating e-commerce revenues from smart-home retail, using third-party payment gateways (Stripe/Shopify) to divert sales proceeds to offshore accounts, or failing to register VAT on cross-border B2C sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act Article 110 – additional tax penalty of up to twice the understated tax amount; Tax Collection Act Article 41 – imprisonment for up to 5 years, detention, or a fine of up to NT$3,000,000 (if fraud is proven).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil can be pierced when the director uses the company as a mere facade. Directors causing fraudulent underreporting are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes, penalties, and interest to the extent of the amount recovered. The Innovation Court may impose civil restitution orders, travel bans (entry control under Article 24 of the Tax Collection Act), and revocation of departure permits. Criminal conviction carries a prison term of 6 months to 5 years, plus personal fines and confiscation of illicit proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion on Non-Resident Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold tax on dividends paid to the mainland China parent, royalties to foreign licensors, or interest to offshore lenders; coercing the payee to refund the withholding benefit or making untaxed remittances through shell companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act Article 114 – withholding agent must pay the unwithheld tax plus a penalty of 3 times the amount. Tax Collection Act Article 42 – criminal liability of up to 3 years imprisonment, detention, or a fine of NT$60,000 or more. For serious fraud, the court may order asset freeze.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who act as withholding agents are personally criminally liable if they knowingly omit withholding or remittance. Individual assets can be attached to cover the shortfall. A blacklisting order restricts the director from leaving Taiwan. In egregious cases, imprisonment is mandatory, and the director also faces disqualification from serving as a directorship in any company for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or submit the required TP report (Local/Master File) when transactions exceed thresholds; creating paper invoices for intercompany service payments without actual service performance or economic substance; using a Hong Kong or BVI shell to park profits while staff remain in Taiwan.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act Article 43-1 and Article 110-1 – re-assessed taxable income at arm's length, resulting in additional tax plus a penalty of 1–2 times the underpaid tax. Under the TP Audit Rules, penalties for non-disclosure of controlled transactions range from NT$3,000 up to NT$30,000 per omission, with further ad hoc adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly allow fictitious transactions can be sued for breach of fiduciary duty; the tax authority may apply the anti-abuse rule to pierce the corporate veil. Directors' personal assets are subject to restitution claims for unpaid corporate taxes. Blacklisting prevents travel until the tax is satisfied. In cases of egregious false documentation, directors face criminal fraud charges under the Criminal Code (Article 210), carrying up to 7 years imprisonment.
